Subject: Dispatcher + storage routing pilot — integration requirements

Hi Mina / Camila,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. VectorStream is keen to run a focused pilot to validate Redwood's dispatcher-based routing between object store (S3) fallthrough and Pinecone as the primary vector store. High-level goals:

- Demonstrate sub-100ms median read for cached prefixes
- Validate graceful degradation to S3 for cold vectors with acceptable P95 latency increase
- Prove cost/throughput characteristics with mixed QPS (bursty search + ingestion)

Attached is a short list of our integration expectations (integration_requirements.pdf). Can you confirm the following so we can scope internal resources on our side?

1) Expected peak QPS you can support for a single index (we're planning for 500 qps initially, up to 2k during bursts).
2) Typical vector size assumptions (we'll be testing 1536 and 3072-dim vectors).
3) Any restrictions on S3 object layout / metadata you expect for fast fallthrough.

We'd like to kick off a two-week technical spike the week of June 7 — can we lock in a 60m joint session with your engs? I've copied Pablo from Pinecone who will help answer their side of the SLA questions.

Thanks,
Sara Holt
Platform Partnerships
VectorStream Inc

Sara — thanks for the doc and clear goals. We're excited to run this with VectorStream + Pinecone. Quick confirmations up front:

- Initial support for 500 qps single-index baseline, with reserved routing lanes for up to 2k qps when on Dedicated.
- We support both 1536 and 3072 vector dims; plan to evaluate memory footprints during the spike.
- S3 layout: prefer objects keyed by 16-byte prefix sharding (format in notes), and minimal per-object metadata; we'll share exact schema.

I've sketched an internal checklist and first-pass rollout plan (redwood_dispatcher_notes.md). Proposed immediate next steps:

1) 60m technical kickoff (please pick a slot via the calendar link) — target week of Jun 7.
2) Share expected QPS patterns and sample vector payloads (VectorStream).
3) We will run a short compatibility test: sample writes to Pinecone + parallel fallthrough reads from S3.
4) Deliver MAP (mutual action plan) within 72h after kickoff.

Can Camila and Dev own the spike execution? Camila — can you draft the compatibility test matrix and include expected tokenization/embedding shape mapping? Dev — can you confirm readiness of the dispatcher staging cluster?

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Partnerships Manager

Adding a few technical constraints and a proposed test matrix.

Key constraints:
- Pinecone index sharding: we prefer 64-shard topology for 2k qps headroom; confirm index name pattern and upsert throughput limits.
- S3 object size: keep objects < 1MB for efficient ranged GETs and parallelization. For large vectors (>1MB serialized) we'll shard on object prefixes.
- KV-cache TTL: we'll test TTLs of 30s, 2m, and 10m to find optimal latency/cost sweet spot.

Compatibility test matrix (draft):
- Phase A (ingest): 10k vectors (mixed dims) -> verify successful upserts to Pinecone and S3 write hashes.
- Phase B (read hot): 10k queries over 5 minutes at 500 qps -> measure median, p95.
- Phase C (fallthrough): Evict cache and run reads expecting S3 fallthrough; measure p50/p95 and IOPS costs.

Drive folder with sample payloads & scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFgHIJ

Camila Reyes
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — Pablo here from Pinecone. A couple of quick notes from our side:

- 500 qps per index is straightforward for our managed plane; 2k qps will need a larger provisioned tier (we can provide a cost estimate).
- Vector dims 1536/3072 will materially change memory; for 3072 we recommend using 16-bit quantization in early tests to reduce RAM footprint.
- For fallthrough scenarios we assume eventual consistency on upserts; we need to agree on acceptable staleness window (suggest 5s for the pilot).

Question for Redwood engs: what are your expected per-request tokenization/embedding sizing (payload bytes) — this affects net egress and P95 on S3 reads. Also, do you intend to batch reads during fallthrough or issue single-vector GETs?

I can prepare a short estimate by tomorrow if you send target QPS + average vector byte size.

—Pablo
BizDev — Pinecone
